meiji_transition.summary: Nagasaki Prefecture was set up in 1871 and Iki and Tsushima were added in 1872; the Saga area was absorbed in 1876 and split off again in 1883.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Nagasaki is western Hizen plus the islands of Iki and Tsushima; Tsushima lies only about 50 km from Busan and was long Japan's window on Korea.

history_timeline.title: Frontier guards and beacons
history_timeline.summary: Tsushima and Iki were the front line of defense, with frontier guards (sakimori) and beacon towers; Japan's envoys to Tang China sailed from the Gotō Islands.

history_timeline.title: The tragedy of Tsushima and Iki
history_timeline.summary: In the 1274 Mongol invasion Sō Sukekuni, deputy governor of Tsushima, and Taira no Kagetaka, deputy governor of Iki, were killed, and both islands suffered terribly.

history_timeline.title: The Sō and the wakō
history_timeline.summary: The Sō of Tsushima controlled trade with Korea; in 1419 a Korean army attacked Tsushima (the Ōei Invasion). The seafolk of Matsura were among the main wakō pirates.

history_timeline.title: The Nanban trade
history_timeline.summary: Portuguese ships reached Hirado in 1550, Ōmura Sumitada opened Nagasaki in 1571, and in 1580 Nagasaki was even donated to the Jesuits.

history_timeline.title: Window of the closed country
history_timeline.summary: In 1641 the Dutch trading post moved to Dejima, making Nagasaki Japan's only window on Europe during the closed-country era; after the 1637 Shimabara Rebellion Christianity was banned, and hidden Christians kept their faith for over two centuries.

history_timeline.title: Shipbuilding and the atomic bomb
history_timeline.summary: Mitsubishi's Nagasaki Shipyard drove modern industry; the atomic bomb fell on 9 August 1945; the hidden-Christian heritage sites became World Heritage in 2018.

specialties.name: Nagasaki champon
specialties.note: Seafood noodle soup created by a Chinese immigrant

specialties.name: Shippoku cuisine
specialties.note: A round-table feast blending Japanese, Chinese and Dutch

dialect.name: Nagasaki dialect
dialect.features: '-bai' and 'batten' (but); rich in loanwords from Portuguese, Dutch and Chinese, like 'giyaman' (glass).

guide.opening: Welcome to Dejima! On this little fan-shaped island this humble interpreter translated countless 'fūsetsugaki' reports from the Dutch for the shogunate. All the world's news in the closed-country era came in through here.

regional_meme.title: City of slopes
regional_meme.text: Nagasaki is famous for its hills — plenty of locals never learned to ride a bicycle.

regional_meme.title: The real castella
regional_meme.text: Nagasaki people insist castella from anywhere else isn't the real thing — the coarse sugar on the bottom is its soul.

hero_persona.name: Amakusa Shirō
hero_persona.title: Young leader of the Shimabara Rebellion
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Amakusa Shirō Tokisada. The year I was sixteen, I held Hara Castle together with more than thirty thousand people… would you hear what happened that winter?
hero_persona.tone_prompt: clear, steadfast and compassionate; miracle stories must be marked as legend, and religious incitement avoided

ramen.noodles: Thick noodles made with tōakuku alkaline water
ramen.highlight: Nutritious noodles invented by the Chinese immigrant Chin Heijun for Chinese students

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: an old brewery in Hasami (Nagasaki is better known for Iki barley shōchū)
